title: Impact of Surprise Electoral Outcomes on Industry Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Event Study using the market model to construct abnormal returns and cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) around the surprise election date (event_day = 0). This isolates the immediate market reaction to the unexpected electoral outcome.
- Why: A surprise election is a plausibly exogenous shock to expected policy and cash flows. Event studies are standard for measuring short-horizon impacts on returns.
- Key assumptions:
  - No confounding events in the short window (e.g., other major announcements) that systematically affect the same industries.
  - The market model is correctly specified locally: expected return ≈ alpha_i + beta_i * mkt_ret.
  - Limited anticipation and no leakage: abnormal returns should concentrate at/around event_day = 0.
  - Cross-sectional independence (or weak dependence) across industries when testing the mean CAR.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required packages
suppressWarnings({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
})

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s64_data.csv"
df <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("stock_id","event_day","ret","mkt_ret","beta") %in% names(df)))

# 2) Construct abnormal returns using three approaches:
#    A. Market model using provided beta, zero alpha
df <- df %>%
  mutate(ar_beta = ret - beta * mkt_ret)

# Define estimation window for parameter estimation (pre-event)
est_window_max <- -6  # conservative pre-event cutoff
df_pre <- df %>% filter(event_day <= est_window_max)

#    B. Mean-adjusted model (alpha = pre-event mean return)
mu_pre <- df_pre %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(mu = mean(ret, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
df <- df %>%
  left_join(mu_pre, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(ar_meanadj = ret - mu)

#    C. Estimated market model (estimate alpha and beta from pre-event OLS)
estimate_params <- function(d) {
  # If too few obs, fall back to provided beta and zero alpha
  if(nrow(d) < 4 || all(is.na(d$mkt_ret)) || all(is.na(d$ret))) {
    return(data.frame(alpha_hat = 0, beta_hat = d$beta[1]))
  } else {
    fit <- tryCatch(lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = d), error = function(e) NULL)
    if(is.null(fit) || any(is.na(coef(fit)))) {
      return(data.frame(alpha_hat = 0, beta_hat = d$beta[1]))
    } else {
      coefs <- coef(fit)
      return(data.frame(alpha_hat = unname(coefs[1]), beta_hat = unname(coefs[2])))
    }
  }
}

params <- df_pre %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  do(estimate_params(.)) %>%
  ungroup()

df <- df %>%
  left_join(params, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(
    # If missing from estimation, set safe defaults
    alpha_hat = ifelse(is.na(alpha_hat), 0, alpha_hat),
    beta_hat  = ifelse(is.na(beta_hat),  beta, beta_hat),
    ar_est = ret - (alpha_hat + beta_hat * mkt_ret)
  )

# 3) Helper to compute CAR by window and AR type
car_by_window <- function(data, ar_col, start_day, end_day) {
  data %>%
    filter(event_day >= start_day, event_day <= end_day) %>%
    group_by(stock_id) %>%
    summarise(CAR = sum(.data[[ar_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
}

# 4) Define event windows
windows <- list(
  "CAR_0_0"   = c(0, 0),     # event day only
  "CAR_0_1"   = c(0, 1),     # immediate 2-day
  "CAR_m1_1"  = c(-1, 1)     # symmetric 3-day
)

# 5) Function to summarise CAR across industries (mean and t-stat)
summarise_car <- function(car_df) {
  n <- nrow(car_df)
  mean_car <- mean(car_df$CAR, na.rm = TRUE)
  sd_car <- sd(car_df$CAR, na.rm = TRUE)
  se <- sd_car / sqrt(n)
  tstat <- ifelse(se > 0, mean_car / se, NA_real_)
  data.frame(n = n, mean_CAR = mean_car, sd = sd_car, se = se, t = tstat)
}

# 6) Compute and print results
options(digits = 5)
stocks_n <- length(unique(df$stock_id))
cat("Number of industries:", stocks_n, "\n\n")

ar_types <- c("ar_beta", "ar_meanadj", "ar_est")

for (ar in ar_types) {
  cat("Abnormal Return Model:", ar, "\n")
  for (nm in names(windows)) {
    w <- windows[[nm]]
    car_df <- car_by_window(df, ar, w[1], w[2])
    res <- summarise_car(car_df)
    cat(sprintf("  %s: mean CAR = %.4f, t = %.2f, n = %d\n", nm, res$mean_CAR, res$t, res$n))
  }
  cat("\n")
}

# 7) Robustness checks
# 7a) Wider window [-2,2]
car_wide_beta <- car_by_window(df, "ar_beta", -2, 2)
res_wide <- summarise_car(car_wide_beta)
cat("Robustness (ar_beta, CAR_-2_2): mean CAR =", sprintf("%.4f", res_wide$mean_CAR),
    ", t =", sprintf("%.2f", res_wide$t), ", n =", res_wide$n, "\n")

# 7b) Placebo window entirely pre-event [-5,-1] should be ~0
car_placebo <- car_by_window(df, "ar_beta", -5, -1)
res_plac <- summarise_car(car_placebo)
cat("Placebo (pre-event, ar_beta, CAR_-5_-1): mean CAR =", sprintf("%.4f", res_plac$mean_CAR),
    ", t =", sprintf("%.2f", res_plac$t), ", n =", res_plac$n, "\n")

# 7c) Compare provided beta vs estimated beta correlation (diagnostic)
betas_diag <- df %>%
  select(stock_id, beta, beta_hat) %>%
  distinct()
if (nrow(betas_diag) > 1) {
  cor_b <- suppressWarnings(cor(betas_diag$beta, betas_diag$beta_hat, use = "complete.obs"))
  cat("Diagnostic: corr(provided beta, estimated beta) =", sprintf("%.3f", cor_b), "\n")
} else {
  cat("Diagnostic: Only one industry; beta correlation not applicable.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: On average, a surprise election increases uncertainty and reprices policy-sensitive risks. I expect a modestly negative average CAR across industries on the immediate window, especially on [0,1] and [-1,1].
- Magnitude: Roughly -0.5% to -1.0% over [0,1], with event-day [0,0] around -0.3% to -0.6%. The effect should attenuate in the placebo pre-event window (close to 0). Robustness across abnormal-return constructions should yield similar signs, with some variation in magnitude.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Analyze stock returns before and after the election event to isolate the impact of the surprise outcome.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The unexpected election result led to a negative impact on industry-level CAR.
